label.en: ● Deep Conceptual Intuition — Functions: Composite & Inverse

body.en: Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental function \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical equations, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the solution set, requiring a final domain check against the original equation.

body.en:
One-to-one condition for inverses: An inverse function \(f^{-1}\) exists if and only if \(f\) is one-to-one over its given domain. For a quadratic function \(f(x) = a(x-h)^2 + k\), the domain must be restricted to one side of the vertex (either \(x \ge h\) or \(x \le h\)). If the domain is all real numbers, the inverse does not exist.

Domain of \(f^{-1}\): The domain of \(f^{-1}\) is always the range of \(f\). Stating \(x \in \mathbb{R}\) when the original function had a bounded range (e.g. \(f(x) \ge 4\)) loses the final mark.

Order of composition: \(fg(x)\) denotes \(f(g(x))\) — evaluate \(g\) first, then insert into \(f\). In general, \(fg(x) \neq gf(x)\). Furthermore, for \(fg\) to be defined, the range of \(g\) must lie entirely within the domain of \(f\).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Functions: Composite & Inverse)

body.en:
Why Completing the Square & Log-Linearization Work: Any quadratic \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \ne 0\)) can be rewritten by factoring \(a\) from the first two terms and adding/subtracting \((b/2a)^2\):

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the range to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

Given \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+1}\) (\(x\geq-1\)) and \(g(x)=2x-3\), find (a) \(fg(x)\), (b) the range of \(fg\).

(a) \(fg(x)=f(2x-3)=\sqrt{2x-3+1}=\sqrt{2x-2}\), domain \(x\geq1\).

(b) As \(x\geq1\), \(2x-2\geq0\), so range of \(fg\) is \(fg(x)\geq0\).

label.en: Worked Example C — Functions: Composite & Inverse (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): In the coordinate plane, the graph of \( y = H(y) \) is translated \( 13 \) units right and \( 7 \) units up to form \( y = K(y) \), mapping \( E(12, 75) \) to \( F \). Find the sum of coordinates of \( F \) on \( y = K(y) \).

Step-by-Step Solution: The image point is \( F(25, 82) \), whose coordinates sum to \( 107 \).

label.en: Worked Example D — Functions: Composite & Inverse (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): The rational function \( H(y) = \dfrac{228y + 25}{12y - 17} \) has horizontal asymptote \( y = K \). Find the asymptote constant \( K \).

Step-by-Step Solution: The ratio of leading coefficients is \( K = \frac{228}{12} = 19 \).

caption.en: Error Diagnosis — Common Student Traps vs. Exam-Board Method (Functions: Composite & Inverse)

rows.en: Confuses the product law \(\ln(xy) = \ln x + \ln y\) with a non-existent sum rule.
Only factor products, quotients, and powers inside logarithms: \(\ln(xy) = \ln x + \ln y\).
Keeping both roots of \(\sqrt{2x+4} = x - 1\) without checking \(x - 1 \ge 0\)
Squaring both sides loses the sign of \(x - {r}\), introducing roots where \(\sqrt{\cdot} = -\text{number}\).
Enforce the range condition \(x \ge 1\) before or after squaring.
Restricting domain of \(f(x) = (x-3)^2 + 1\) to \(x \ge 0\) for invertibility
The vertex is at \(x = 3\), so \(f(2) = f(4) = 2\) fails the horizontal line test on \(x \ge 0\).
Restrict the domain at the vertex axis of symmetry: \(x \ge 3\) (or \(x \le 3\)).

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — Functions: Composite & Inverse

body.en: Fast Exam Check (Cambridge International AS Level (9709 Paper 1 / Paper 4 / Paper 5)): To verify an inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\) in 5 seconds, pick a simple input \(x_0\), compute \(y_0 = f(x_0)\), and check that \(f^{-1}(y_0) = x_0\). Also verify that the graph of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) reflects \(y = f(x)\) across \(y = x\).

question.en: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 13\) for \(x \ge 3\). (a) State the range of \(f\). (b) Find an expression for \(f^{-1}(x)\) and state the domain and range of \(f^{-1}\).

solution.en:
(a) Complete the square: \(f(x) = (x - 3)^2 - 9 + 13 = (x - 3)^2 + 4\). Since \(x \ge 3\), \((x - 3)^2 \ge 0\), so the minimum value is \(f(3) = 4\). The range of \(f\) is \(f(x) \ge 4\).
(b) Set \(y = (x - 3)^2 + 4\). Rearrange for \(x\): \[y - 4 = (x - 3)^2 \Rightarrow x - 3 = +\sqrt{y - 4} \quad (\text{since } x \ge 3)\] \[x = 3 + \sqrt{y - 4}\] Therefore, \(f^{-1}(x) = 3 + \sqrt{x - 4}\).
Domain of \(f^{-1}\) is \(x \ge 4\) (the range of \(f\)), and range of \(f^{-1}\) is \(f^{-1}(x) \ge 3\) (the domain of \(f\)).

question.en: Functions \(g\) and \(h\) are defined by \(g(x) = 2x - 1\) for \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), and \(h(x) = \dfrac{6}{x - 2}\) for \(x \neq 2\). (a) Find an expression for \(hg(x)\) in simplest form. (b) Solve the equation \(hg(x) = g(x)\).

solution.en:
(a) Substitute \(g(x)\) into \(h\): \[hg(x) = h(2x - 1) = \dfrac{6}{(2x - 1) - 2} = \dfrac{6}{2x - 3} \quad \left(x \neq \tfrac{3}{2}\right)\] (b) Set \(hg(x) = g(x)\): \[\dfrac{6}{2x - 3} = 2x - 1 \Rightarrow 6 = (2x - 1)(2x - 3)\] Expand the right-hand side: \[6 = 4x^2 - 8x + 3 \Rightarrow 4x^2 - 8x - 3 = 0\] Factor: \((2x - 3)(2x + 1) = 0\).
Since \(x \neq \tfrac{3}{2}\) for \(hg(x)\) to be defined, the value \(x = \tfrac{3}{2}\) is excluded.
Therefore, the unique solution is \(2x + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\).

question.en: [Practice 3 · Medium] A piecewise function is defined by \( H(y) = 3y + 11 \) for \( y < 3 \) and \( H(y) = y^2 + K \) for \( y \ge 3 \). Find the parameter \( K \) that makes \( H(y) \) continuous at \( y = 3 \).

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Functions: Composite & Inverse and start from \( H(y) = 3y + 11 \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( y = 3 \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

solution.en: Continuity at \( y = 3 \) requires \( 3(3) + 11 = 3^2 + K \implies K = 11 \).

question.en: [Practice 4 · Hard] Consider the quadratic function \( H(y) = 10y^2 - 21 \) over the closed interval \( [2, 12] \). Find the average rate of change \( \Delta H / \Delta y \) on \( [2, 12] \).

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Functions: Composite & Inverse and start from \( H(y) = 10y^2 - 21 \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( \frac{H(12) - H(2)}{10} = 10((12) + 2) = 140 \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

solution.en: The average rate of change is \( \frac{H(12) - H(2)}{10} = 10((12) + 2) = 140 \).
